note: One file per dataset. Every number states where it came from, so adding a dataset means writing its reference down rather than editing code, and every difference from that reference is listed rather than inherited by accident.

reference.name: Claude Code + DeepSeek-V4-Pro
sources: Per-task scores: metadata/index.parquet of huggingface.co/datasets/FrontisAI/NatureBench-traces, rows where harness=claude-code and model=deepseek-v4-pro, column effective_improvement; each value cross-checked against that case's own submissions.jsonl and all 90 agree
Protocol: the leaderboard entry deepseek-v4-pro-claude-code states 'solvingBudget: 4 h / task', 'externalAccess: Web search and web fetch tools disabled', and one GPU per GPU task
Copy of the index committed at config/swarmrsi/naturebench_traces_index_20260919.parquet

observed_behaviour.note: It never stops early: the median run is a minute over its own budget, and it keeps improving until the clock ends. Any early stop of ours makes the two runs incomparable.

deviations: Backbone is deepseek-flash through DeepSeek's own API, not deepseek-v4-pro through OpenRouter. A cell of ours is therefore not a same-backbone comparison.
Hardware is one NVIDIA H200 (141 GB) per cell against the reference's 24 GB or 80 GB. We have more, and say so.

The stop target is the leaderboard's Surpass-SOTA bar rather than the reference score. The reference does not stop early at all, so stopping when we merely clear it would report where we crossed a line against where they ran out of time.
Campaign counts are unlimited because the published protocol is a wall clock and nothing else; declaring counts the reference was not held to is a constraint we would be inventing.

per_action_counts_are_not_null_here_beca: Measured on this benchmark's own cells, not borrowed. Across 138 completed NatureBench cells, those spending 12 or fewer calls per action carry a median best of -0.021 against -0.093 for those spending 13 to 18, and land 90% of their actions against 67%. Within a task, calls per action correlates -0.23 with the result and action count -0.18, while scored actions (+0.13) and evaluations (+0.12) are what track it: landing scored programs helps, spending longer on each attempt does not. One task run six times across a day of widening peaked at 16 and fell at every step; at 48 it spent 82 minutes on two actions and both failed. The other five counts stay null because the published protocol is a wall clock and nothing else; these two are set because this benchmark's own cells say where the useful range is.
inherited_and_wrong: Thresholds scraped from the leaderboard page's bundled JavaScript. The regex anchored on the first "id" in a window before the entry, which was gpt-5-4-codex, so all 88 values were Codex + GPT-5.4. An eighteen-task panel was run and reported as 0/18 against them; against the intended reference the same cells stand at 6/18. Use the index, never the page.

parallel_tool_calls: false. No provider serving this model on OpenRouter accepts the parameter, so sending it with provider.require_parameters routes to zero providers and returns HTTP 404. It is also inert where it does route.
The 150-call campaign budget. Fourteen of eighteen cells reached it in fifty to sixty minutes with three of their four hours unspent, against a reference that had the full four.
